q: My LO is currently fighting sleep like crazy and just screams for hours until he falls asleep. Tonight I just broke down and literally sobbed whilst he screamed on me.
c: Mother of a 4-month-old on the night she posted.

q: I hadn’t washed my hair in 9 days and washed it today and felt guilty that my LO had to sit in his bouncer for 15 minutes whilst I quickly washed and dried it.
c: Guilt over fifteen minutes to herself.

q: My LO nana came over to help out yesterday as I had 2 hours sleep in 36 hours but all he did was scream for me.
c: Grandmother's help didn't settle the baby.

q: My partner works, but in a way I have started to envy him. He has a bath everyday, plays PlayStation, sits on his phone.
c: Mother envies her working partner's free time.

q: I do every single bedtime routine, so I’m pretty much trapped from 6-onwards. I do the bedtime feed and the next 2, my partner takes the early one then goes to straight to work

q: I definitely think dads don’t feel as much guilt you are right about that! It almost annoys me watching him but it really isn’t harming anyone, I guess it’s just jealousy of the freedom I once had without feeling guilty.
c: Same mother, in a reply.

q: He doesn't do well with gentle reassurance without picking him up, he won't stay lying down if I sit beside the cot rubbing his back/hand, if I go in and put his soother back in and not pick him up it gets thrown at me and screaming starts again
c: First-time mother of an 18-month-old with new bedtime tantrums.

q: I hate having to wake him but I'll try anything now for a chance at easier nights.
c: Mother agrees to cap naps.

q: So we thought, she’s getting too much sleep during the day and that’s why she can’t sleep at night. But now her sleep is just a complete disaster with many hours of screaming and demanding constant attention in the middle of the night.
c: A week after moving a 17-month-old to one nap: 2–3 hour night screams.

q: How long did this messy phase last for you? Did your baby adjust after a few days/weeks or did it take longer?
c: Parent asks how long adjustment takes.

q: We think she might now be thinking of her bedtime as ‘first nap’ and wanting a full 3-4hr wake window in the middle of the night
c: Parent's theory of the split night.

q: We are first time parents and feeling a bit overwhelmed and was hoping someone can help us out with our little ones schedule as we are feeling a bit defeated at the moment.
c: First-time parents of a 14-week-old on all-contact naps.

q: I’m so sorry for the late reply, these last few days/weeks have been absolute hell for us […] I’ve been tracking his sleep and the last two days were very rough. I’ve provided them below and was hoping if you have time if you could please take a look.
c: Six weeks later the parent returns to the same commenter with two days of minute-by-minute logs.

q: The problem is that 6:00am is normally when we start our day. I’ve been trying to follow age-appropriate wake windows and keep total daytime sleep to around 3 hours, so I’m not sure what to do.
c: Four weeks on, a bad night breaks the plan.

q: I’ve been doing cio since baby turned 6 months. She is now 8 months old today and her falling asleep independently is a disaster. Scream crying for 30 minutes with ww adjust shorter, longer you name it.
c: Two months of CIO with no improvement.

q: Okay I figured it was a consistency thing and I just have to push through.
c: Parent accepts the 'consistency' answer.

q: I tried Ferber before and she’s the type of baby to ramp up the crying with check ins that don’t involve picking up
c: Check-ins made this baby worse.

q: Thank you so much for the example schedule and explanation! I’ll try the by the clock method that seems less stressful.
c: A commenter's by-the-clock schedule.

q: Let’s say she finally falls back asleep now, do I still do the regular suggested schedule of 630 wake, 3.5/4/4 ww, 2.5 max of nap time even tho she’ll only get 9hr15min night sleep? It’s currently 305am
c: First night on the new schedule, posting at 3am.

q: it means we get zero time to ourselves. we go from work to baby care to bed. it’s mentally killing me.
c: First-time mother of a 9-month-old who now needs rocking.

q: can anyone offer non-cry it out methods? I’m okay with some whining but I can’t just let him cry until he passes out
c: She states her limit.

q: a first time mom just trying not to mess this kid up
c: Her sign-off.

q: we’ve been using the huckleberry sleep function to give us estimated sleep times. this week I switched to manual wake windows.
c: Same mother, cross-post: she dropped the app's predictions.

q: he is suddenly fighting bedtime SO hard. it can take easily 2 hours and he seems to be pushing bed time to 8 or 9, which is ridiculous. he MUST be rocked to sleep.
c: After teething, bedtime takes two hours.

q: I took a half day at work today so I could nap while my family helped with him because I’m so tired I feel like I can barely see straight.
c: Parent of a 9-month-old waking every 45 minutes.

q: I often see him dozing off for 1–2 seconds, then startling himself awake and we start again. […] Then he becomes overtired and escalates into full crying that he can’t calm down.
c: Parent of an 18-week-old with long wake windows.

q: Most guidance I’ve seen suggests 2 naps at 6 months the earliest, but he’s not even 5 months yet.
c: The baby doesn't match the guidance.

q: I think he might be getting into some kind of overtired cycle, but I don’t know how to prevent it. […] It feels like a vicious circle.
c: Same parent in a reply.

q: This was working fine until the last 3 weeks when he fights bedtime until after 10. Our bedtime routine is now pushing 2 hours of me laying with him fighting for my life.
c: Working mother of a just-3-year-old with low sleep needs.

q: I asked them to please stop the nap and was told they legally need to offer him a nap. I asked to.please, for the love of god, wake him up after 30 min. They said nope.
c: Daycare refuses to shorten the nap.

q: I work. My son being up until after 10 is making it impossible to do ANYTHING at all. I have no time to clean, no time with my husband, no time for myself. Im at my breaking point.
c: Same mother.

q: Im trying to find a new center but I live in a rural area with not many options and the wait lists are longer than he would even attend since prek starts in September
c: No other daycare option.

q: Unfortunately this kid has never once fallen asleep independently since he entered this world […] im not sure how they get him to do it at daycare.
c: Daycare manages what home cannot.

q: I feel like I made him go through all of that crying for nothing by picking him up at the third wake up. I don’t have the heart for this. But I also can’t mentally go on with this level of sleep deprivation.
c: Parent of a nearly 5-month-old after night 1 of Ferber.

q: My mental health is taking hit no matter the route.
c: Same parent.

q: I was just going to buy her course for 5 months I tried her 3 month course and it didn’t work because he’s so high needs and needs to be rocked
c: Parent bought one age course that failed and is about to buy the next.

q: We actually didn’t stop Ferber and night 3 he only needed 20 minutes of occasional crying to fall asleep which was a win.
c: Two days later: night 3 went well.

q: He had the worst night he’s had in awhile. He woke up crying every 2 hours ugh
c: The same night 3.

q: At two or three in the morning, whenever the baby cries, I have to get up to attend to her […] She can sleep during the day,but I still have to go to work, day after day.
c: A father who takes the nights and still works days.

q: To be honest, while I’m caring for the baby and watching my wife sleeping in the middle of the night, I do feel a little uncomfortable. However, she takes care of the baby during the day, so this is just a bit of petty moods from me.
c: Same father on his resentment.

q: Sometimes I walk around holding her until my arms ache from patting her back, but she just stares right back at me with wide-open eyes.😭
c: Same father.

q: I can admit that we’ve created some bad sleeping habits and sleep associations for our son due to pure exhaustion and lack of knowledge.
c: First-time mother of a 4.5-month-old.

q: How long does it take to break these habits and associations? Do we change one thing at a time or just do a complete reset and mess everything up just to fix it?
c: She asks for the order and timeline.

q: I feel like I’m freshly postpartum with the nighttime scaries again with how much I’m dreading nights these days 🫩
c: Dread of nights returns.

q: She is previously sleep trained but we’ve resorted to bad habits after she got sick so she is now waking every hour overnight. We tried to retrain tonight and she scream cried for 30+ minutes at bedtime and we gave up.
c: Parent of a low-sleep 8-month-old: illness undid training; the retrain stopped on night one.

q: I’ve once heard someone say if your baby cries that hard that long at bedtime, they’re undertired. Could this be possible for her?
c: A rule of thumb the parent has heard.

q: I have no idea how I would add any more awake time as there’s already so much.
c: Same parent.

q: She has never slept through the night (closest we’ve come was two nights ago where she slept 8pm-4am! I cried haha).
c: Mother of a just-turned-one on her best night.

q: Honestly writing this all out made me realise I probably just need to get her sleeping independently and night weaned…
c: Writing the post clarified the plan.

q: I walk out of the room and he does not stop crying, screaming and now he’s making him self throw up!
c: A 2-year-old scared of monsters cries until he vomits.

q: I tell his dad to sit in the chair by his bed and not pick him up but he doesn’t listen. He rocks him and tries to put him in his bed a few times
c: The father won't follow the agreed plan.

q: Monster spray doesn’t work…. Cracked door doesn’t work, night light doesn’t work. Bribing him doesn’t work!
c: Every toddler trick tried.

q: It shouldn’t be this hard. He used to smile when I laid him in his bed but now he panics.
c: Same parent, two weeks in.
